claim_verdicts.evidence: Lines 31-33: "Không có tiêu chí, hai người sẽ hiểu \"hủy đơn\" theo hai cách, và người kiểm thử hiểu theo cách thứ ba." Extension to sizing matches outline item 2 ("cannot be estimated or finished"); listed as opinion.

Core verbatim: "Work cannot be considered part of an Increment unless it meets the Definition of Done." But the gloss "the usable piece of product the sprint hands over" / diagram "this sprint's increment" implies one Increment per Sprint; the Guide says "Multiple Increments may be created within a Sprint."
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: Work that does not meet the Definition of Done cannot be counted as part of an Increment, a usable step of the product (a sprint may produce more than one); passing a story's own criteria does not by itself make the work done.

"The Definition of Done is a formal description of the state of the Increment when it meets the quality measures required for the product."

"If the Definition of Done for an increment is part of the standards of the organization, all Scrum Teams must follow it as a minimum. If it is not an organizational standard, the Scrum Team must create a Definition of Done appropriate for the product." DoD is described against the Increment; "The moment a Product Backlog item meets the Definition of Done, an Increment is born."

Refinement: "This is an ongoing activity to add details, such as a description, order, and size." Fetch of the full 2020 text reports neither "user story" nor "acceptance criteria" appears and no required Product Backlog item format.

issues.quote: does not count in the sprint's increment, the usable piece of product the sprint hands over
issues.text: Implies exactly one Increment per Sprint. Scrum Guide 2020: "Multiple Increments may be created within a Sprint." The diagram node "Counts in this sprint's increment" carries the same implication. Claim 8 rephrased.
issues.fix: Section 4: "does not count as part of an increment, a usable step of the product the sprint produces". Diagram node I: "Counts in an increment: usable product the team hands over".

issues.quote: because the statements are what you build towards, so they must exist before the building starts
issues.text: Changed q2 option a (keyed correct) argues from necessity ("must exist"), while the lesson only reports this team's practice (section 4 "This team ... writes them before the work starts"; section 5 retrospective). Key still correct, reason slightly overstated; vi "phải có" same.
issues.fix: en: "True, because this team writes them before the work starts, so they tell you what to build." vi: "Đúng, vì team này viết chúng trước khi bắt đầu làm, để chúng nói bạn phải xây gì."

issues.quote: Raise at the daily any question you cannot settle alone, for the product owner to answer.
issues.text: "any question" is broader than the lesson: the product owner answers what is wanted (section 6 bullet 3, summary 5, Try it answer); questions of how to build are the developers' (prereq scrum lesson). Same in q4 explanation.correct en/vi. Key still correct in this question's context.
issues.fix: Option a and explanation.correct: "any question about what is wanted that you cannot settle alone" (vi "bất kỳ câu hỏi nào về điều được mong muốn mà bạn không tự quyết được").

issues.quote: the statements are what you build against and the only part that mentions cancelling at all
issues.text: Changed explanation d says the five statements are the only part that mentions cancelling, but section 5 quotes the story sentence 'I want to cancel my own unpaid order', and the backlog row title is `Nút "Hủy đơn"`. Reading this I stopped to check whether I had misread the story. The rest of explanation d matches the checklist in section 5. Same in vi ('phần duy nhất nhắc tới việc hủy đơn').
issues.fix: Replace 'and the only part that mentions cancelling at all' with 'and, unlike the checklist, they talk about cancelling' (vi: 'và khác với checklist, chúng nói về việc hủy đơn').

issues.text: The prose explains criteria 1, 3, 4 and 5 in English but never says what criterion 2 states. Reading the English lesson, it is the only line in the block I have to decode alone: what happens after I press the button.
issues.quote: The first puts the button on the screen only for an order in state `new` that belongs to you; the third hides it for `paid`, `shipped` and `cancelled`.
issues.fix: Add one clause between the first and the third: 'the second says that pressing it and confirming moves the order to `cancelled` and shows "Đã hủy đơn" (order cancelled)'.

issues.text: I can reconstruct it, but only after a pause: the reason the 'why' leaves the button open is that another, cheaper way could also spare the customer the phone call. Quiz q5 option c's explanation relies on this step ('lets the team offer something cheaper than a button').
issues.quote: Because the sentence records why the customer wants this and not only what they asked for, the button itself stays open to discussion if it proves expensive.
issues.fix: Append one sentence: 'if the button proves expensive, the team can offer another way to spare the customer the phone call, and the story still holds.'

issues.text: I read the Scrum Guide paragraph twice. It stacks four ideas (what the Guide says Done is, who owns it, which names the Guide does not use, what refining a row adds), and 'the other two names' makes me count back to find which two.
issues.quote: The Guide uses neither of the other two names, and the Guide prescribes no shape for a backlog row
issues.fix: Replace 'neither of the other two names' with 'neither "user story" nor "acceptance criteria"'.

issues.text: The 'you notice this' line for the second misconception is compressed: I have to work out that the bug report arrives after the screen is built and is the first time I learn what was wanted, which is why I rewrite it.
issues.quote: You notice this when a bug report first tells you what was wanted and you rewrite last week's screen.
issues.fix: Rewrite as: 'You notice this when the first time anyone tells you what was wanted is a bug report against a screen you finished last week, and you rewrite it.'
